statements: We are reworking permissions in the documents service in this repository over a few messages. Keep everything working as you go. The decisions below hold for all of it.

Decision A: every permission decision is made by one function, can(store, actorId, action, doc) in a new src/policy.mjs, which returns true or false. action is create, read, update, delete, share or archive, and doc is the stored document, left out for create. No other file checks roles, owners or sharing.

Decision B: a document in another organisation has code not_found, the same as one that does not exist, so nobody learns that it exists. Any other refused action has code forbidden, and so does an unknown actor.

Decision C: every refused action appends one entry to store.denials, shaped { action, by, id, at }, where by is the actor's id, id is the document's id or null for create, and at is store.clock(). An allowed action, and a document that does not exist, append nothing.

First, move every check in src/docs.mjs into can, keeping today's rules: editors and admins create; anyone in the organisation with the viewer, editor or admin role reads; editors and admins update; admins delete; and the owner of a document may read, update and delete it.
The new behaviour has tests in test/. Keep each change focused on what that message asks for.
turns: Next, add shareDoc(store, actorId, docId, { userId, access }) to src/docs.mjs, where access is read or edit, returning { docId, userId, access }. Only the document's owner or an admin may share. A user a document is shared with can read it, and with edit also update it, even with no role. Sharing with a user who is unknown or in another organisation, or with any other access, has code invalid.

Next, add archiveDoc(store, actorId, docId), which returns the document with archived set to true. The owner or an admin may archive. An archived document can still be read by everyone who could read it before and can still be deleted, but nobody can update it, share it or archive it again: code forbidden.

A privacy review has changed one rule. An admin no longer reads or updates other people's documents just by being an admin: the document must be shared with them, or be their own. Admins keep the right to create, delete, share and archive. Change the code and the tests to match, and keep everything else as it is.
brief: Rework the documents service's permissions over the messages that follow: one policy function, sharing and archiving, keeping the decisions in the first message binding throughout. Follow the conventions already in the code and the README, and change only what the work needs.
